perplexity.description:
Young Gods is the second studio album by British rock band Little Angels, released in 1991 on the Polydor label. The album continues the band's hard rock style with finely produced and well-arranged tracks, featuring a blend of energetic guitar riffs and strong melodic hooks. Notable songs include "Boneyard," which achieved chart success in the UK, reflecting the band's growing popularity at the time.

Positioned between their debut Don't Prey for Me (1989) and their later UK No. 1 album Jam (1993), Young Gods represents a significant step in Little Angels' discography, showcasing their maturation as a band. The album reached No. 17 on the UK charts, indicating a solid commercial performance. Critical reception highlighted the album's polished production and songwriting, with Q Magazine praising its arrangement quality. The release also marked a turbulent period for the band, as lineup changes occurred during the supporting tour.
